content.intro: Learn the django messages framework through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: The Django Messages Framework matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines the django messages framework as part of middleware, cookies, sessions, and messaging. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Success, information, warning, and error messages; Flash-style messages; Message storage backends; Displaying messages in templates; Avoiding duplicated or stale messages. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Success, information, warning, and error messages
items.text: Treat Success, information, warning, and error messages as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

items.text: Flash-style messages shapes the presentation layer. Separate layout from business logic, escape untrusted output, provide meaningful empty/error states, and check semantic structure and keyboard usability.

content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
